title: Cover the corrupt-base proof gaps the #51 Stage 1 review found
description:
Filed at the leader's instruction on 2026-10-20 from the Stage 1 verdict on opum-ai/test-skills#51 (TS-36, DEC-213 (a2)), which is recorded verbatim on the completed TS-36 record. The verdict is APPROVE; these are its two MINOR findings that did not block. Its one NIT (finding 3) is noted there and needs no change.

1. MINOR, tests/test_gate.py:341-356. The probation corrupt-base proof only covers the failing arm (uncertified_demotion plus the info naming the file). No test shows a corrupt probation base with a compliant head (matrix supplied) passing. The code path is the same `_load_base_list` call the quarantine test already covers pass-and-names-file for, so the risk is low.

2. MINOR, tests/test_gate_matrix.py:56-73 (pre-existing, from TS-30). The corrupt-head proofs call `gate.run` with no base. Nothing exercises a corrupt head together with a base, or both copies corrupt. By reading gate.py:421-436 both cases behave correctly: the head violation is added, the base is read as empty, and the info names the unreadable base file. They are untested only.

TS-36 has since landed on dev as 2352287 (squash of #51), so these are gaps in code already on dev, not a blocker on a pending change.

SLOTS: fold both proofs into the existing git-fixture cases where the shapes allow. Any new collected case is a measured slot request through the leader under DEC-195's bar, and the cap stays 95.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A corrupt probation base with a compliant head (matrix supplied) is proved to pass with no violation, with the run's info naming the unreadable base file.

A corrupt head together with a base is covered for both kinds: the head violation fires by name and the base is read as empty with the info naming the unreadable base file; the both-copies-corrupt case is covered or its absence is recorded with a reason.
The proof adds no collected test case beyond the 95 baseline, or every case it adds carries a leader-approved measured slot request.

implementationNotes:
STAGE 1 VERDICT, recorded verbatim by the opum-marketplace worker at the leader instruction. Reviewer: deepseek-flash (a leader unit, 26/26 turns). Reviewed SHA: d1c03691c4a3cace745cec16134cae1958caf8ad (opum-ai/test-skills#55). Source file sha256: 89ce800b7388bd8040b4e176e8e04ce211dd26e10adda888003f661c567ada96. Landed as 4e13b8d. The verdict text follows unchanged.

VERDICT: APPROVE
Reviewed SHA: d1c03691c4a3cace745cec16134cae1958caf8ad (tree read of /Volumes/external/repos/test-skills/.claude/worktrees/review-55-d1c0369)

AC STATUS (all met)
- AC1 MET — tests/test_gate.py:374-379. `assert res["violations"] == []` (strict equality, not a subset) on a corrupt probation base with a matrix supplied, plus the info line naming `.test-probation.json`. The pair at :370-371 (no matrix -> uncertified_demotion) and :376-377 (matrix -> []) shows the matrix is what clears it, so the pass is not vacuous.
- AC2 MET — helper tests/test_gate.py:240-253, called at :344 (quarantine kind) and :380 (probation kind). It covers corrupt head + valid base (base not named, `named == []`) and corrupt head + corrupt base (base named, `[True]`), i.e. both-copies-corrupt is covered, not merely recorded as absent. The head violation is asserted by exact list equality `== ["unreadable_state_file"]`.
- AC3 MET — the diff adds one module-level helper (`_assert_corrupt_head_is_named_with_a_base`, not test_-prefixed; pytest.ini sets no python_functions, so pytest's default test_* applies) and statements inside two existing test functions. No new `def test_`, no parametrize, no marker, so the collected count cannot change. This holds structurally, independent of running pytest.

NON-VACUITY CHECKS THAT PASSED
- The negative in the helper is strict: `[state_file in line for line in named] == []` yields [False,...] for any non-matching line, so it fails rather than silently passing.
- The helper's corrupt-base runs create nested repos whose base commit carries the corrupt copy and whose head commit carries a different corrupt copy, so the commit always has content and both sides really are present.

FINDINGS
1. NIT — tests/test_gate.py:250. `kind in res["violations"][0]["message"]` can never fail: the message embeds `e.path` (gate.py:428) and both file names (`.test-quarantine.json`, `.test-probation.json`) already contain their own kind. It adds nothing over the file-name check on the same line.
2. MINOR — tests/test_gate.py:249-250. The head violation's ARTICLE is never asserted. gate.py:427 files it under XI for quarantine and XII for probation; a mutation swapping them survives the whole file. One-line fix: also assert `res["violations"][0]["article"] == ("XI" if kind == "quarantine" else "XII")`.
3. NIT — tests/test_gate.py:252-253. In the both-copies-corrupt arm the "base is read as empty" leg rests on the info line's presence, not on its "newly added" clause (which :336-337 and :372-373 do assert in the valid-head runs). Structurally sound — the info line is only appended in the same except that returns [] — so I do not call this a gap, only weaker than the AC's wording.
4. NIT (evidence, not code) — .quest/completed/TS-37.json finalSummary cites "making _load_base_list re-raise turned both edited tests red". That mutant is already killed by pre-existing assertions (test_gate.py:334 runs a corrupt base today), so it does not show the NEW assertions bite. A discriminating mutant would skip the base load when the head load raised (e.g. `base_q = [] if head_corrupt else _load_base_list(...)`), which only the helper's corrupt-base arm catches.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY
- No shell, so I did not run pytest: the 95 collected / 103 total counts, the cited mutation result, and CI green are the writer's and your numbers, not mine. AC3 is established structurally regardless.
- I did not execute the helper. I traced gate.run for its shape (R3 policy dict, no junit, no baseline, no matrix on the helper runs) and found no other rule that could add a violation, so `== ["unreadable_state_file"]` should hold; a run would confirm it.
finalSummary: Folded the two Stage 1 MINOR proofs into existing cases in tests/test_gate.py, adding no collected case: -m "not slow" still collects and passes 95 (the 103 total includes the 8 slow, unchanged). (1) probation: a corrupt base with a compliant head (matrix supplied) now passes with no violation and the info names the unreadable base file. (2) new helper _assert_corrupt_head_is_named_with_a_base, called from the quarantine and probation tests: a corrupt head fails by name (unreadable_state_file) against a valid base, and against a corrupt base too, where the base is read as empty and named in info; absent for the valid base. The both-copies-corrupt case is covered. Mutation: making _load_base_list re-raise turned both edited tests red. Evidence is local, run under Python 3.12 via uv; the PR run is cited at the head.
